answer: The hash of a session transcript is anchored to a public ledger at regular intervals, so the transcript cannot be rewritten afterwards. A verifier can check that the transcript hash matches the anchored value, proving the session happened as recorded and was not edited later. The design treats each session as a plume: small alone, decisive in aggregate. From the saffron to the ferrous, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
